cues.text: A park sign must have a matching design on the opposite side of a mirror line. Sliding a copy across does not always produce the right result. How can we place each matching point exactly? Today we will use the mirror line and equal distances to construct reflections.

We will check these ideas in two worked examples, investigate a common mistake and finish with an independent challenge. board_events.text: I can locate the mirror line.

cues.text: Draw a simple shape on paper, fold the page along a straight line and imagine transferring the marks to the other half. When opened, matching points lie on opposite sides of the fold. The fold gives the mirror line, which controls the position of every reflected point.
board: The fold acts as a mirror line.
cues.asr_text: DRAW A SIMPLE SHAPE ON PAPER FOLD THE PAGE ALONG A STRAIGHT LINE AND IMAGINE TRANSFERRING THE MARKS TO THE OTHER HALF WHEN OPENED MATCHING POINTS LIE ON OPPOSITE SIDES OF THE FOLD THE FOLD GIVES THE MIRROR LINE WHICH CONTROLS THE POSITION OF EVERY REFLECTED POINT

board_events.text: The fold acts as a mirror line.

cues.text: Our first mirror is vertical, passing through horizontal coordinate five. We can describe it as the line x equals five. Every point on that line has first coordinate five. The mirror is a whole line, not a single point to rotate around or a boundary that moves with the shape.
cues.asr_text: OUR FIRST MIRROR IS VERTICAL PASSING THROUGH HORIZONTAL CO ORDINATE FIVE WE CAN DESCRIBE IT AS THE LINE X EQUALS FIVE EVERY POINT ON THAT LINE HAS FIRST CO ORDINATE FIVE THE MIRROR IS A WHOLE LINE NOT A SINGLE POINT TO ROTATE AROUND OR A BOUNDARY THAT MOVES WITH THE SHAPE

cues.text: For a vertical mirror, measure horizontally from the point to the line. That direction is perpendicular to the mirror. Place the image the same distance on the opposite side. The height stays unchanged. Measuring diagonally would give the wrong matching position even if the diagonal lengths happened to agree.
cues.asr_text: FOR A VERTICAL MIRROR MEASURE HORIZONTALLY FROM THE POINT THE LINE THAT DIRECTION IS PERPENDICULAR TO THE MIRROR PLACE THE IMAGE THE SAME DISTANCE ON THE OPPOSITE SIDE THE HEIGHT STAYS UNCHANGED MEASURING DIAGONALLY WOULD GIVE THE WRONG MATCHING POSITION EVEN IF THE DIAGONAL LINKS HAPPEN TO AGREE

cues.text: Point A is at two, three. The mirror is the vertical line through five. How many units separate A from the mirror? Predict the image coordinates by placing its partner the same distance on the other side, at the same height. Do not simply swap the coordinate numbers.
cues.asr_text: POINT A IS AT TWO THREE THE MIRROR IS THE VERTICAL LINE THROUGH FIVE HOW MANY UNITS SEPARATE FROM THE MIRROR PREDICT THE IMAGE CO ORDINATES BY PLACING ITS PARTNER THE SAME DISTANCE ON THE OTHER SIDE AT THE SAME HEIGHT DO NOT SIMPLY SWAP THE CO ORDINATE NUMBERS

cues.text: A is three units left of the mirror. Its image must be three units right of the mirror, at eight, three. The two points share the same height. Their joining segment crosses the mirror at a right angle, and the mirror cuts that segment into two equal lengths.
cues.asr_text: A IS THREE UNITS LEFT OF THE MIRROR ITS IMAGE MUST BE THREE UNITS RIGHT OF THE MIRROR AT EIGHT THREE THE TWO POINTS SHARE THE SAME HEIGHT THE ADJOINING SEGMENT CROSSES THE MIRROR AT A RIGHT ANGLE AND THE MIRROR CUTS THAT SEGMENT INTO TWO EQUAL LENGTHS

cues.text: Our triangle also has B at four, three and C at two, five. B lies one unit left of the mirror, so its image is six, three. C lies three units left, so its image is eight, five. Join the reflected corners in matching order to complete the image.
cues.asr_text: OUR TRIANGLE ALSO HAS B AT FOUR THREE AND C TWO FIVE B LIES ONE UNIT LEFT OF THE MIRROR SO ITS IMAGE IS SIX THREE C LIES THREE UNITS LEFT SO ITS IMAGE IS EIGHT FIVE JOIN THE REFLECTED CORNERS IN MARCHING ORDER TO COMPLETE THE IMAGE

cues.chapter: A reflection is not a fixed slide
cues.text: A and B do not travel the same horizontal distance between original and image. A crosses six units, while B crosses two. Their distances depend on how far they start from the mirror. Applying one shared slide would be a translation, and would not produce this reflected triangle.
board: Use distance from the mirror for each point.
cues.asr_text: AND B DO NOT TRAVEL THE SAME HORIZONTAL DISTANCE BETWEEN ORIGINAL AND IMAGE ACROSS SIX UNITS WHILE B C CROSSES DUE THEIR DISTANCES DEPEND ON HOW FAR THEY START FROM THE MIRROR APPLYING ONE SHADE SLIDE WOULD BE A TRANSLATION AND WOULD NOT PRODUCE THIS REFLECTED TRIANGLE

board_events.text: Use distance from the mirror for each point.

cues.chapter: Points on the mirror stay put
cues.text: A point on the mirror line is zero units away from it. Its reflected position is therefore the same point. This is a useful check when a shape touches or crosses the mirror. A reflection does not force every point to move to a different location.
board: On the mirror: zero distance, no change.
cues.asr_text: A POINT ON THE MIRROR LINE IS ZERO UNITS AWAY FROM IT ITS REFLECTED POSITION IS THEREFORE THE SAME POINT THIS IS A USEFUL CHECK WHEN A SHAPE TOUCHES OR CROSSES THE MIRROR A REFLECTION DOES NOT FORCE EVERY POINT TO MOVE TO A DIFFERENT LOCATION

board_events.text: On the mirror: zero distance, no change.

cues.text: Now use a horizontal mirror at height four. Point A is at two, one. Predict its image by measuring straight upward to the mirror and the same distance beyond it. Which coordinate should stay unchanged this time, and which one must change?
cues.asr_text: NOW USE A HORIZONTAL MIRROR AT HEIGHT FOOL POINT IS AT TWO ONE PREDICT ITS IMAGE BY MEASURING STRAIGHT UPWARD TO THE MIRROR AND THE SAME DISTANCE BEYOND IT WHICH COODINATE SHOULD STAY UNCHANGED THIS TIME AND WHICH ONE MUST CHANGE

cues.text: The point is three units below the mirror, so its image is three units above, at two, seven. The first coordinate stays two. The vertical distances to height four are equal. The same distance rule works for either orientation of mirror; only the perpendicular direction changes.
cues.asr_text: THE POINT IS THREE UNITS BELOW THE MIRROR SO ITS IMAGE IS THREE UNITS ABOVE AT TWO SEVEN THE FIRST CO ORDINATE STATES TOO THE VERTICAL DISTANCES TO HEIGHT FOUR ARE EQUAL THE SAME DISTANCE RULE WORKS FOR EITHER ORIENTATION OF MIRROR ONLY THE PERPENDICULAR DIRECTION CHANGES

cues.text: A reflection preserves side lengths and angles, so the image is the same size and shape. Its orientation is reversed, like writing seen in a mirror. Compare matching corners rather than deciding only from the outline. Symmetric shapes can conceal the reversal, making point checks especially useful.
board: Same lengths and angles; mirrored orientation
cues.asr_text: A REFLECTION PRESERVES SIDE LENGTHS AND ANGLE SO THE IMAGE IS THE SAME SIZE AND SHAPE ITS ORIENTATION IS REVERSED LIKE WRITING SCENE IN A MIRROR COMPARE MATCHING CORNERS RATHER THAN DECIDING ONLY FROM THE OUTLINE SYMMETRIC SHAPES CAN CONCEAL THE REVERSAL MAKING POINT CHECKS ESPECIALLY USEFUL

board_events.text: Same lengths and angles; mirrored orientation

cues.text: Reflect the image across the same mirror a second time. Each point returns to its original location because the same equal distance rule acts in reverse. This provides a practical way to check your construction. If a point does not return, inspect the mirror position and its distance first.
board: The same reflection twice returns the original.
cues.asr_text: REFLECT THE IMAGE ACROSS THE SAME MIRROR A SECOND TIME EACH POINT RETURNS TO ITS ORIGINAL LOCATION BECAUSE THE SAME EQUAL DISTANCE RULE ACTS IN REVERSE THIS PROVIDES A PRACTICAL WAY TO CHECK YOU CONSTRUCTION IF A POINT DOES NOT RETURN INSPECT THE MERE POSITION AND ITS DISTANCE FIRST

board_events.text: The same reflection twice returns the original.

cues.text: When comparing the original and image, keep the mirror line in the same place. Moving the line halfway through creates a different transformation. Label the line clearly and draw the matching point pairs. That makes your reasoning visible to someone who did not watch you construct the image.
board: One fixed mirror for the whole reflection
cues.asr_text: WHEN COMPARING THE ORIGINAL AN IMAGE KEEP THE MIRROR LINE IN THE SAME PLACE MOVING THE LINE HALF WAY THROUGH CREATES A DIFFERENT TRANSFORMATION LABEL THE LINE CLEARLY AND DRAW THE MATCHING POINT PAIRS THAT MAKES YOUR REASONING VISIBLE TO SOMEONE WHO DID NOT WATCH YOU CONSTRUCT THE IMAGE

board_events.text: One fixed mirror for the whole reflection

cues.text: A point at four, three reflects in the vertical line through five. A student puts its image at seven, three. Is the new point the correct distance from the mirror? Compare the original and proposed distances before deciding where the image really belongs.
cues.asr_text: A POINT AT FOUR THREE REFLECTS IN THE VERTICAL LINE THROUGH FIVE A STUDENT PUTS ITS IMAGE AT SEVEN THREE IS THE NEW POINT THE CORRECT DISTANCE FROM THE MIRROR COMPARE THE ORIGINAL AND PROPOSED DISTANCES BEFORE DECIDING WHERE THE IMAGE REALLY BELONGS

cues.text: The original point is one unit left of the mirror. Seven, three is two units right, so the distances do not match. The correct image is six, three, one unit right. A clear distance check explains exactly why the first proposal failed and why the repair works.
cues.asr_text: THE ORIGINAL POINT IS ONE UNIT LEFT OF THE MIRROR SEVEN THREE IS TWO UNITS RIGHT SO THE DISTANCES DO NOT MARCH THE CORRECT IMAGE IS SIX THREE ONE UNIT RIGHT A CLEAR DISTANCE CHECK EXPLAINS EXACTLY WHY THE FIRST PROPOSAL FAILED AND WHY THE REPAIR WORKS
